title: Heightened Concerns and Measures with Local Transmission of COVID-19
what_it_is: Heightened Concerns and Measures with Local Transmission of COVID-19

sections.label: COVID-19 case numbers
sections.summary: As of 17 February 2020, there were 70,548 confirmed cases and 1,770 deaths in mainland China, 881 cases and five deaths outside, and 77 local cases with 24 recovered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As of 17 February 2020, based on the World Health Organization’s report, globally, there are 70,548 confirmed cases in mainland China with 1,770 deaths, and 881 confirmed cases outside of mainland China with five deaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Locally, as of 17 February 2020, we have 77 confirmed cases of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Twenty-four cases have fully recovered from the infection and have been discharged from hospital.

sections.label: Public Health Preparedness Clinics activated
sections.summary: The Public Health Preparedness Clinics were activated to strengthen primary care defences to better detect and manage COVID-19 cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Today, we activated the Public Health Preparedness Clinics (PHPCs) to strengthen our defences at the primary care front to better detect and manage COVID-19 cases.

sections.label: Five-day medical certificates guidance
sections.summary: MOH gave doctors guidance to provide five-day medical certificates for patients with respiratory symptoms so they can stay home to rest and recover.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) has, therefore, given guidance to doctors to provide medical certificates (MCs) of five days for patients with respiratory symptoms so that they can and should stay home to rest and recover quickly.

sections.label: Advice to church organisations
sections.summary: Church organisations were advised to continue services, minimise unnecessary social interactions, take temperatures, and remind unwell members to stay home and rest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For church organisations, for example, we have advised them to continue with their services, minimise unnecessary social interactions so as to minimise contact to prevent transmission within the church and to also continue to take temperature and remind members that if they are unwell, they can stay at home and rest rather than to come to church.

sections.label: Temperature screening at gatherings
sections.summary: Temperature screening remains an important measure to prevent ill people from joining activities and mass gatherings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Temperature screening remains one of the very important parts of the measures that we have put in place to prevent people who are ill from joining activities and participate in mass gatherings.

sections.label: Consult doctor for mild symptoms
sections.summary: Singaporeans feeling unwell with respiratory symptoms like coughing and running nose are encouraged to consult a doctor, particularly an activated PHPC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In the beginning part, when you are in the initial phase, your symptoms may be very mild but you do carry viral load and you can still be infectious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, we encourage Singaporeans who feel unwell, especially with the symptoms that I had mentioned, respiratory symptoms – coughing, running nose and so on – to please consult a doctor, particularly with PHPC, now that we have activated them.

sections.label: Five-day medical certificate guidance
sections.summary: Doctors are given guidance to issue a five-day medical certificate so patients can rest at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: If not, doctors are given guidance to give you a five-day MC so that you can rest at home.

sections.label: Temperature-taking precautionary measures
sections.summary: Temperature-taking is stated to be an important part of precautionary measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: To answer the Member's question, temperature-taking is an important part of our precautionary measures.

sections.label: No DORSCON Red plans
sections.summary: The speaker repeats that there are no plans to go to DORSCON Red.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Just for avoidance of doubt, let me repeat this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have no plans to go to DORSCON Red.

sections.label: Stay-Home Notice enforcement resources
sections.summary: The passage asks what enforcement resources exist for Stay-Home Notice compliance and notes technology is used to monitor people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, what are the enforcement resources that the Government has at its disposal to ensure that returnees actually comply with the requirements of the Stay-Home Notice?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We do not have an estimated total number of people returning because it depends on the decision of the individuals, whether or not they intend to return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Many of these, who are on Stay-Home Notices, are required to stay at home and we are leveraging technology as well to monitor them.

sections.label: Stay-Home Notice spot checks
sections.summary: People on Stay-Home Notice must stay home all the time and are spot-checked through telephone calls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For the Stay-Home Notice, they are required to stay home all the time and we will do spot checks on them through telephone calls and so on, to make sure that they are at home.

sections.label: Closed chat groups monitoring difficulty
sections.summary: A person was found to be choked rather than having COVID-19, and closed chat groups are difficult to monitor.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But what we found out was that there was no COVID-19, the person actually was choked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This is a very difficult challenge because they are, by nature, closed chat groups, it is very difficult for us to monitor.

sections.label: Testing 30,000 flu-like cases daily
sections.summary: About 30,000 people daily have flu-like symptoms, and testing them finds only five to 10 cases, which is not very helpful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Every day, we have about 30,000 people down with flu-like symptoms, such as running nose, cough, cold and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In the end, every day, we find about five to 10 cases, as Members have seen in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, to find this five to 10 cases every day by testing 30,000 is not going to be very helpful.

sections.label: Staying home first five days
sections.summary: The strategy is to encourage the individual to stay at home for the first five days so the body can recover.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: If not, our strategy is to encourage the individual to please stay at home for the first five days so that your body will be able to recover.

sections.label: Clarification on MC days guideline
sections.summary: A request for clarification that the number of days given is a guideline, not mandatory, and up to doctors and frontline healthcare personnel.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can we just get clarification and reinforcement that it is really not mandatory, but it is a guideline, a recommendation, but it is really up to the doctor and the frontline healthcare personnel as to how many days we want to give?

sections.label: Guidelines footnote on doctors' judgement
sections.summary: The footnote of the guidelines says doctors are to exercise judgement and decide how many days to be given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: It is important to read the footnote of our guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And the footnote does say that "doctors are to exercise judgement and to decide how many days to be given".

sections.label: Appeal to employers on five-day MC
sections.summary: An appeal to employers to allow employees to go on the five-day MC if given five days of MC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: At the same time, we also want to take this opportunity to appeal to employers to allow the patient – your employees – to go on the five-day MC if he is given five days of MC.

sections.label: Fatality numbers in China
sections.summary: In terms of fatality, the numbers today show that in the whole of China it is about 2% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In terms of fatality, the numbers today show that in the whole of China, it is about 2% to 3%.

sections.label: Living with H1N1 long term
sections.summary: The passage says the situation looks like H1N1 and that people need to expect to live with it for a long time, noting H1N1 infected over 400,000 Singaporeans in a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are watching them, but this is as it stands today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, it looks more like H1N1, we do need to expect to live with it for quite a long time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: H1N1 has infected more than 400,000 Singaporeans in Singapore alone within a year.

sections.label: Habit and vulnerable groups
sections.summary: The passage says living normally with precautions is a habit to inculcate and asks about vulnerable groups such as the elderly whom the state is trying to protect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, I think it is a habit that we should inculcate today and live life as normally as possible and take necessary precautions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I want to ask about the more vulnerable groups, such as the elderly, whom I understand, of course, the state is trying to protect.

sections.label: Alternatives for elderly activities
sections.summary: The passage describes elderly people queueing for food packages but no longer eating together, and suggests splitting groups and part-time activities as alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Maybe they will queue up to get food packages, but they do not get to sit down to have meals together anymore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I am wondering if there is an alternative to this while protecting them, for example, splitting them so that there are not more than a hundred in a group and maybe have some part-time activities so that they can actually continue to have a platform where they can be educated and updated on the latest news and be encouraged to exercise or maybe co-clean some shared facilities and so forth.

sections.label: Restarting activities with precautions
sections.summary: The passage says some organisations need time to manage activities, and assures Ms Denise Phua that organisations will be worked with to restore as many activities as possible and practicable with precautions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Some organisations may need time to work out exactly how to manage some of these activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, I assure Ms Denise Phua that we do want to work with the organisations which are overseeing these activities to put back as many of these activities as possible and practicable while taking necessary precautions, particularly all the health promotion activities and exercises.

sections.label: HPB and VWO restarting activities
sections.summary: The passage says the Health Promotion Board and voluntary welfare organisations may take time to study the situation and put precautions in place, and are encouraged to restart soon, with some possibly congregating in coffee shops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) as well as the various voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) may take some time to study the situation, put in place the necessary appropriate precautions and we encourage them to restart as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And instead of coming to the SACs, some of them may congregate in the coffee shops, which has the same effect of mixing.

sections.label: Stay-Home Notice and three levels
sections.summary: The passage says Stay-Home Notices are enforceable to minimise community exposure, and lists three levels: confirmed cases in hospitals, close contacts under quarantine orders, and China returnees under Stay-Home Notices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We want to minimise the risk of exposing them to the community and, therefore, we have this Stay-Home Notice which is enforceable and requires them to be at home all the time until the notice period is over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, there are actually three different levels: (a) those who are confirmed cases, they are in hospitals; (b) those who have close contacts with confirmed cases, they are of a higher risk and they are served quarantine orders; and (c) those who are returning from China, have been exposed in China, but no direct contact with known cases and these are served with Stay-Home Notices.

sections.label: Confirmed cases are real
sections.summary: The cases determined as confirmed are real cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The cases that we have determined as confirmed are real cases.

sections.label: Surveillance and case detection
sections.summary: Doctors make ground assessments, and proactive and sentinel surveillance are used to pick up cases that would otherwise go unnoticed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, we will leave it to the doctors to make their ground assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But the Member is right that it is not possible to detect 100% of the cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We do proactive surveillance, meaning we look at all possible cases of pneumonia and some non-pneumonia cases we also investigate to see whether we are able to pick up cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We also have a sentinel surveillance programme, which means we actually randomly pick patients in the community to test for potential respiratory infections, including COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This will allow us to pick up cases that would otherwise have gone totally unnoticed.
